title: Tenant hash-clash leading to eviction amplification and memory growth - follow-up
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Summary: During a mixed-tenant burst on 2026-02-23 we observed sustained memory growth and a tenant-scoped outage for two customers. Root cause analysis shows a hash-clash sensitivity introduced by a change to the tenant sharding hash in release runtime-1.19 plus an eviction scoring oscillation under bursty access patterns. The hash-clash increased local collision rates, causing prefetched entries to frequently map to the same slab set. That combination amplified eviction churn, prevented efficient TTL reclamation, and produced effective memory growth for affected shards. This ticket tracks remediation, telemetry gaps, mitigations, and rollout plan.
comments: 2026-02-24: Initial incident detected by Alerts team: kvcache_shard_memory_growth > 85% for shard-22 and shard-73. Pager duty alerted on high memory + evictions spike. - Aisha K.

2026-02-24: On-call (Marco C) confirmed eviction_rate doubled and hit read latency regressions. Temporary mitigation: increased eviction backoff and triggered partial drain of shard-22. Noted correlated recent rollout: runtime-1.19 tenant-hash migration (canary group).

2026-02-25: Postmortem kickoff meeting. Decided immediate mitigation and longterm fixes: (1) roll back tenant-hash change for canary cohort, (2) add per-tenant hash entropy probe and alert, (3) implement eviction hysteresis to avoid oscillation under hotspot churn. Action owners assigned. - Meeting notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/notes/ENG-783210-pm

2026-02-27: Root cause draft: hash migration used truncated fingerprint that reduces collision entropy for small tenant keyspaces. When tenant footprints are similar across many requests, collision increases and prefetch/evict interactions thrash the same slab buckets. Added repro harness to kvcache-integration tests (PR linked).

2026-03-01: Engineering design decided: revert hash truncation and replace with per-tenant salt + 64-bit fingerprint. Also implement eviction hysteresis: require score to exceed threshold for N consecutive windows before eviction, and add short-term admission control for prefetch to avoid fill storms. Design doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/documents/kvcache-eviction-hysteresis-design

2026-03-03: PRs created: github.com/redwood-inference/kvcache/pull/4123 (revert hash truncation), github.com/redwood-inference/kvcache/pull/4180 (eviction hysteresis + prefetch throttle). Tests added: deterministic collision simulation and tenant-scale soak. - Marco C

2026-03-05: Telemetry gaps identified: no existing alert for per-tenant collision rate, no histogram for consecutive-eviction-windows. Added metrics: kvcache.tenant_collision_rate, kvcache.eviction_hysteresis_missed_count. Instrumentation PR: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/129

2026-03-07: Canary revert deployed to canary cohort (10% of fleet) and observed normalized collision_rate and 40% reduction in eviction churn for affected shards during load sweep. No customer-facing regressions observed. - Deployed by SRE ops runbook link: https://runbooks.redwood.ai/kvcache-rollbacks

2026-03-09: Long-term follow-ups agreed: (A) Add admission controls for prefetch under tenant-hotspot conditions, (B) Add deterministic fuzz test for hash collision patterns to CI, (C) Add cross-tenant isolation telemetry & run periodic tenant-shard entropy scans. Owners and ETA assigned below.
2026-03-10: Validation: soak test across representative tenant mix for 48h shows memory stable and eviction churn within baseline. Planning phased rollout to remaining fleet next week. - Marco C
action_items: Revert hash truncation in runtime-1.19 and replace with 64-bit salted fingerprint (owner: Marco Chen, ETA: 2026-03-12)
Implement eviction hysteresis with consecutive-window check and backoff (owner: Priya Nair, ETA: 2026-03-18)
Add prefetch admission-control: limit prefetch insertion rate per-tenant under high eviction pressure (owner: Daniel Ortiz, ETA: 2026-04-01)
Add telemetry: kvcache.tenant_collision_rate, eviction_hysteresis_missed_count, per-tenant slab-occupancy percentiles (owner: Telemetry team, ETA: 2026-03-10 - instrumentation merged)
Create deterministic hash-collision fuzz harness and add to CI presubmit (owner: QA Eng, ETA: 2026-03-25)
Publish a runbook for this class of incident including automated detection and escalation playbook (owner: SRE, ETA: 2026-03-15)
Schedule a cross-team retrospective and update onboarding docs to highlight hash migration risk patterns (owner: Aisha Kapoor, ETA: 2026-03-22)
risks: Rollbacks can affect performance for tenants who relied on truncated hash distribution; performance regressions must be measured in canary before full rollout.
Eviction hysteresis could delay cleanup under real memory pressure if thresholds misconfigured; must tune with production-like load tests.
Prefetch admission controls risk slightly increased cold-start latency for some sequences; trade-off accepted to prevent memory storms.
tests_and_validation: Added deterministic collision simulation and stress harness to kvcache-integration (PR #4123).
Soak test: 48h representative tenant-mix run with synthetic hotspots; observed stable mem and eviction metrics.
Canary metrics: collision_rate metric dropped by ~65% in canary cohort; eviction churn reduced ~40% during sweeps.
CI change: collision fuzz harness will run nightly; presubmit added for PRs touching tenant hashing logic.
notes: This ticket is intentionally scoped to address the immediate regression and systemic telemetry & CI gaps. Separate follow-up tickets will track long-term isolation improvements and capacity planning changes.
